# reports/

## Flight_Operations_Dashboard.html

The standalone executive dashboard — a single self-contained HTML file, bilingual
(Arabic RTL / English), no build step, no server.

**This file is generated, not edited.** Its aggregate blob is produced by
`scripts/build_dashboard.py`, which imports every rule from
`scripts/flight_rules.py`, asserts the result against the published baselines,
and refuses to write if any assertion fails.

### Setup

The template is not yet in this folder. Copy it in once:

```bash
cp ../Flight_Operations_Dashboard.html reports/
```

Then regenerate:

```bash
python scripts/build_dashboard.py --data data/raw
```

### The red banner

If the dashboard shows a red banner across the top, its data was not produced by
`build_dashboard.py` — or was produced by a run whose assertions failed. The
banner names the specific problem. It disappears on a clean regeneration.

The banner exists because of what happened to the previous version of this file:
it was generated by code carrying its own copy of the on-time rule, that copy
used `> 15` where the model uses `>= 15`, and it published 14,206 flights in the
wrong status. Nothing about the page looked wrong. A dashboard that has drifted
from its model should say so on its own face rather than wait to be caught in a
meeting.

### Do not hand-edit the numbers

Correcting a figure by hand creates a third copy of the truth, which is the
problem this whole arrangement exists to prevent. Change the rule in
`flight_rules.py`, run `validate_dataset.py`, then regenerate.
